key_evidence_accepted: The ballistic report connecting the pistol recovered from the appellant with the bullet recovered from the body of the victim is an inculpatory fact.
witness_credibility: There are no eyewitnesses to the crime, implicating the appellant. The case against the appellant rests entirely on circumstantial evidence.
bail_history: The appellant was granted bail by this Court on suspension of sentence, vide order dated 08.04.2024. The bail bonds and sureties furnished by the appellant shall be treated as cancelled.
trial_duration: Dates of offence: 13.11.2011; Trial judgment: 18.10.2022; High Court decision: 18.10.2022; Supreme Court decision: 19 September 2024
legal_representation: Ms. Shweta Garg, Ashish Gopal Garg, Rakesh Garg, Advs. for the Appellant; Nachiketa Joshi Sr. Adv./A.A.G., Pashupathi Nath Razdan, Pushpender Singh, Mirza Kayesh Begg, Ms. Maitreyee Jagat Joshi, Ms. Ruby, Advs. for the Respondent
investigation_status: FIR registered, charge sheet filed, trial completed
appeal_history: Trial court: Conviction of Nirbhay Singh @ Rajesh Mama, Jitendra Singh, and the appellant; High Court: Acquittal of Jitendra Singh, upheld conviction of appellant; Supreme Court: Appeal allowed, conviction set aside
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the ballistic report connecting the pistol recovered from the appellant with the bullet recovered from the victim's body is an inculpatory fact. They also claimed that the discovery and recovery of the pistol was attributable to the disclosure statement provided by the co-accused, and that the prosecution may take the benefit of Section 8 of the Evidence Act.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the absence of corroborative evidence directly linking the appellant to the crime introduces a significant gap in the chain of circumstances, failing to establish a hypothesis of guilt that conclusively excludes all other reasonable possibilities.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the principle that where the case rests entirely on circumstantial evidence, a finding of guilt is justified only if all incriminating facts and circumstances are incompatible with the accused's innocence, and there is a complete chain of evidence excluding all other possibilities.
precedent_relied_upon: Hanumant v. State of Madhya Pradesh [1952] 1 SCR 1091 : (1952) 2 SCC 71; Sharad Birdhichand Sharda v. State of Maharashtra [1985] 1 SCR 88 : (1984) 4 SCC 116; Perumal Raja v. State, Represented By Inspector of Police [2024] 1 SCR 87; Mohmed Inayatullah v. State of Maharashtra [1976] 1 SCR 715 : (1976) 1 SCC 828; State of Maharashtra v. Suresh [1999] Supp. 5 SCR 215 : (2000) 1 SCC 471
other_sentence_order: The appellant was granted bail by the Court on suspension of sentence, and the bail bonds and sureties furnished by the appellant shall be treated as cancelled.
